answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a stake-backed identity bridge. Each agent locks collateral before its vote counts, and the bridge binds one deposit to one signing key, so minting N fake identities needs N separate bonds. The pool sits in a slashable harbor: an agent caught double-voting loses its stake. An attacker's cost scales linearly with every clone and stays at risk, while an honest agent risks just its own bond. A plume of cheap bots cannot clear the deposit gate, so influence must be bought with real capital.
